newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill Pakistani Shi'ite local leader.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill Pakistani Shi'ite local leader.

text.p: Masked gunmen fatally shot a Shi'ite Moslem lawyer in Pakistan's Punjab province on Saturday and his minority sect blamed a rival militant group from the majority Sunnis, police said.

The two gunmen, who escaped on a motorcyle, shot Ishtiaq Hussain Bokhari, president of Lodhran district bar association and the local chief of the Shi'ite Tehrik-i-Jafria group, at Kror Pakk sub-district town in southern Punjab, the police said.
Tehrik officials accused the Sunni Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP) group for the shooting. No SSP comment was immediately available.
The two groups have accused each other of a series of deadly attacks on their members and mosques in Punjab and North West Frontier province in recent months.
Sunni-Shi'ite disputes over Islamic beliefs have often spilled into violence. Sunnis predominate in Pakistan's population of about 130 million and Shi'ites constitute about 15 percent.
